# HerculeRadar glossary

## Mention

One public post that matched a monitor's keywords. Deduplicated on
(project, source, external id), so a post matching three aliases is one mention.

## Categories

- `bug_report` — Bug report. Something is broken. Usually the most time-sensitive category.
- `complaint` — Complaint. Unhappy, but not a defect — pricing, support, policy.
- `misinformation` — Misinformation. A factual claim about the product that appears untrue.
- `product_idea` — Product idea. A feature request or a wish, however casually phrased.
- `testimonial` — Testimonial. Unprompted praise, quotable with the author’s permission.
- `other` — Other. Relevant but none of the above. The model is never forced to guess.

## Sentiment

`positive` / `neutral` / `negative`, from the author's point of view about
the brand — not the tone of the post in general.

## Urgency

0-100, scored by consequence rather than by tone. Public outrage, security
claims, viral misinformation and blocked paying customers score high. A passing
positive remark scores low. 70 and above is worth interrupting a person for.

## Relevance

`is_relevant: false` means the keyword matched by coincidence — a different
company, a common word, spam. These are stored with status `ignored` and are
excluded from alerts and webhooks. Relevance rate is the honest measure of
whether the monitor's keywords are well chosen.

## Status

`new` → `reviewed` → `done`, or `ignored`. Status is the only mutable
field on a mention; everything else is a fact about the post.

## Sources

- `x` — X
- `reddit` — Reddit
- `youtube` — YouTube
- `linkedin` — LinkedIn
- `threads` — Threads

## Limits

Collection is capped by the plan's mention quota. Reaching it pauses collection
and returns `USAGE_LIMIT` (HTTP 402) on writes that would collect more; reads
keep working. Nothing is billed as overage automatically.
